_comment: Hand-curated, PUBLIC-DOMAIN Tier-A seed for the Qurʾān↔poetry comparison feature. Source: Arabic Wikisource (classical, pre-modern verse — public domain). This is a STARTER anchor, not the full corpus: the bulk of the Jahilī material comes from the Kaggle scrape (Tier C) promoted by `poetry_corpus.py tiers`. Expand this file from a critical edition over time. Tatweel/kashida is stripped on load (and was stripped here).

poems.title: معلقة امرئ القيس
poems.source_ref: Muʿallaqa of Imruʾ al-Qays — Arabic Wikisource
poems.notes: The most famous opening in Arabic poetry; the nasīb / aṭlāl (weeping at the abandoned campsite). Anchors the motif-inversion examples (cf. Q 27:52).

lines.hemistich1: قِفَا نَبْكِ مِنْ ذِكْرَى حَبِيبٍ ومَنْزِلِ

lines.hemistich2: فَهَلْ عِنْدَ رَسْمٍ دَارِسٍ مِنْ مُعَوَّلِ
عَلَى النَّحْرِ حَتَّى بَلَّ دَمْعِي مِحْمَلِي

lines.hemistich1: ألاَ رُبَّ يَوْمٍ لَكَ مِنْهُنَّ صَالِحٍ

poems.title: معلقة لبيد بن ربيعة
poems.source_ref: Muʿallaqa of Labīd ibn Rabīʿa — Arabic Wikisource
poems.notes: Labīd is the bridge poet (he later embraced Islam). Opening is the aṭlāl. Line 4 uses the root ر-ز-ق (rizq).

poems.title: بيت لبيد المفرد (ألا كل شيء)
poems.source_ref: Labīd — first hemistich cited in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6403 as the truest line a poet ever spoke
poems.notes: The CONTINUITY anchor (research doc §4.5): a pre-Islamic poet voicing near-tawḥīd. The Prophet praised the first hemistich. Used to prove the feature surfaces agreement, not only contrast.

lines.hemistich1: أَلَا كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مَا خَلَا اللَّهَ بَاطِلُ
